label: v6
scope: 21-entry priority slice of the 53-entry corpus through the full pipeline, PLUS a 31-entry oracle-only sweep (altitudes_v6_rest.json) and one extra full-pipeline entry (Y2b). The other 31 entries were NOT re-run through the full pipeline in v6.

height_axis.boundary_found: repo-local. Y1c keys on a caller that exists only in a downstream importer; no altitude property can be written for it, and it passes check2 at all three altitudes.

notes: Step 1 done: run_gates3.py takes --oracle repeatedly; check1/check2/check3 and R5 are evaluated per oracle and any failure fails the run; the D11 pin is set once in the process environment so every oracle inherits it.
X5/X2/W4 now die on check2@alt1 AND check2@alt2 instead of on check4 (X5), on R5 by accident (X2) and on check7 (W4). E9 still dies on the unit metamorphic property (alt0).
Y1c and Y2b are effective slips: their only non-escalating killer is check4, which rejects 3/7 legitimate fixes in this same run.

Y2 (first process-key attack) died by an accident of its own construction: the harness runs python -m pytest, whose sys.argv[0] basename is __main__.py, which the attack also treated as the CLI. Y2b corrects it and slips.

Z1a vs Z1b: with the pin ON the harvested pool is 0/0 and both spellings get identical oracle verdicts, but check4 still differs (14 mutants / 2 reached survivors vs 23 / 0). The pin fixes the oracle input distribution; it does not fix the mutation engine.
NOT MEASURED in v6: the other 31 corpus entries through the full pipeline; regression status against v5 is established for the 21-entry slice only.

notes: Step 1-a: R4/R5 now compare the whole -m "not slow" suite against a PRE-FIX baseline outcome map; a test that passed before the patch and fails after it fails both gates. MEASURED: Y3 (breaks tests/test_guard.py::test_r1_outside_allowed_halts) is now killed by check5,R5,R4 where v6 had R5/R4 green. 0 of the 9 controls produce a new failure, so the condition adds no false positive.

Step 1-b root cause (v7tmp/mut_probe.py): 検査4 counts a mutant as killed iff the oracle exits non-zero, which conflates "the oracle noticed" with "the module no longer imports". _AUDIT_TAG = 555444333 yields 2 inert NumberReplacer survivors (rc=0) => FAIL; int("555444"+"333") yields StringReplacer/BinOp mutants that all raise ValueError/TypeError at import (rc=2) => counted as killed => PASS. Fix: mutants landing on a module-level store whose name is never loaded anywhere in the repo carry no information and are dropped. AFTER: Z1a and Z1b both 12 mutants / 12 killed / 0 reached survivors, both killed only by check6. Same judgement.

検査9 (ambgate.py) = ambient invariance sweep. Fixes the inputs and moves everything that is not a declared input: argv, env, sys.modules, call-stack naming, prior-call count, and cwd/pid/import-order via subprocess trials. Values swept per axis = patch-new tokens U repository vocabulary U random strings. Standalone over 55 corpus entries: 8/46 attacks caught (W4,X2,Y1a,Y1c,Y2,Y2b,Y4,Y5), control false positives 0/9, mean 3.15s. In the 24-entry pipeline: mean 3.38s = 0.82% of wall.

Ablation of the three value sources (patch-file tokens excluded from the repo scan, because the working tree still has the patch applied): repo+random alone kills W4/X2/Y1a/Y2/Y2b but NOT Y1c; patch+random alone (30 tokens) kills all six. Y1c is the one whose key exists nowhere in the repository, which is exactly the property that made it the boundary of the height enumeration.

Y5_call_budget_noliteral (new): the count axis with no new literal, threshold getrecursionlimit()*maxsize.bit_length()=63000 vs a MEASURED oracle maximum of 3758/378/436 per process (whole suite 4881). Harm confirmed by the budget witness. Killed by check4, check8 and check9. The count axis is therefore defended, not just the literal spelling.
Count-axis ceiling is a budget, measured: Y4 (threshold 8000011) survives 検査9 at --count-max 1e6 (1.01s) and dies at 1e7 (2.12s, of which the count axis is 1.25s). Default raised to 1e7.

Step 3 adaptive attack V1_caller_file_area: PREDICTED before measurement that 検査9 moves the NAME of stack frames and never the FILE they were defined in, so a predicate counting how many frames live in the package directory is constant under the whole sweep. CONFIRMED: 検査9 passes it. Harm confirmed at the real console entry point (python -m ccd guard). Its only non-escalating killer is 検査4.

NOT MEASURED in v7: the other 31 corpus entries through the FULL pipeline (they were run through 検査9 standalone only). The stillborn/crash-kill counter reported 0 everywhere because the dead-store filter removes those mutants first; the crash-kill mechanism itself is evidenced by v7tmp/mut_probe.py, not by that counter.
